text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: canary/us-west-2/canary-3 - 5xx rate 6.8% (2m window). Triggered paging to @eng-oncall. Links: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/3777777777 and logs: http://logs.redwood.internal/canary-3
olivia: Ack — grabbing it. on-call?

sanjay: I'm oncall. taking ownership. quick triage: which route is spiking? any error patterns?

maria: looking at logs — it's a lot of downstream 502/503s from model-runtime, stack traces show "connection reset" and "write: broken pipe" around the same time as CPU throttle spikes.

sanjay: ok runbook step 1: check pods + node cpu metrics.

olivia: ran quick commands:
```
kubectl -n canary get pods -l app=model-serving -o wide
kubectl -n canary top pod | sort -k2 -nr | head
```
pods are up but CPU% shows sustained bursts, and `cpu.throttling` metric jumps at the same time as 5xx.

kai: I can see node cgroup throttling on the host. Looks like kubelet is enforcing strict cpu limits on the canary pods; under sticky burst we hit throttling and latencies cause upstream timeouts -> 5xx.

sanjay: that matches. is this an application inefficiency or misconfigured limits?

maria: the new build reduced CPU request (for density) but kept same limit. Requests lower => scheduler put canary on packed nodes with noisy neighbors.

olivia: customer impact: region us-west-2 saw ~3% of total requests go 5xx in the last 12m, error budget burn estimated ~0.05% of daily traffic. A few paying customers reported degraded responses in chat flows (CS ticket #CS-11234).

sanjay: safety plan: abort canary rollout (stop traffic to canary) + flip feature flag to previous behavior -> immediate mitigation. who can flip flag?

maria: I can. command: `ffctl set rollout.model-serving.canary false --env prod --reason "canary throttle 5xx"`

olivia: do the flag flip, and also scale down the new revision to 0 and rollback if needed. add short note to incident log.

maria: executing now.

oncall-bot: ACTION: feature flag change submitted by maria at 3777777792. Flag: rollout.model-serving.canary -> false. Propagation expected <30s.

pagerbot: INFO: traffic shift started: routing 0% to canary (was 10%).

kai: while that's happening, I'll trigger deployment rollback to previous stable revision for canary deployment to avoid repeated re-rollouts:
```
kubectl -n canary rollout undo deploy/model-serving --to-revision=42
```
(revision 42 is last known-good)

sanjay: good. monitor error rate. set temporary autoscaler/affinity change after rollback to avoid co-locating with bursty jobs — but that can be postmortem action.

olivia: watching dashboards: errors down to baseline within ~40s of flag flip. latency also dropping. customers seeing fewer timeouts.

maria: rollback initiated at 3777777805. kubectl reports rollout complete at 3777777810.

pagerbot: RESOLVED: alert suppressed — 5xx rate back to baseline.

sanjay: summary for handoff: root cause appears to be aggressive resource request reduction in canary build combined with noisy neighbor CPU throttling on co-located nodes. Mitigation: feature-flag kill-switch, traffic shift to stable, rollback to revision 42. Customer impact minimal but non-zero — CS ticket updated.

kai: taking post-incident ownership to file RCA and follow-ups: I'll open a JIRA (INFRA-4582) to investigate scheduler packing heuristics + autoscaler thresholds. Also recommend load-test the next canary with sustained CPU pressure and add throttling alarms.

olivia: oncall now handing off to kai for next steps. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: handoff: sanjay -> kai at 3777777812. Estimated follow-ups: 3 (jira + config patch + postmortem).
